title: 14th Sitting of Third session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 27 members present and took up a no-confidence motion against Mohamed Saeed, Minister of Economic Development, Transport and Trade. Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir presented the motion, which 13 MPs signed on 3 August 2026. It accused the minister of letting the black-market dollar rate rise, port congestion, spending on investor forums abroad without disclosing results, stalled megaprojects, and Special Economic Zone (SEZ) amendments that it said put sovereignty at risk. The minister used his hour to reply point by point. He said the Maldives Monetary Authority sets exchange-rate policy, more dollars are now released at the official rate, the port is moving to Thilafushi, and bunkering earned USD 90.07 million. In the members' debate, PNC MPs backed the minister and MDP MPs pressed the case against him. The debate continues into part 2, and no vote is recorded in this part. This part finishes the debate on the motion of no confidence in Economic Development, Transport and Trade Minister Mohamed Saeed. Government-side members defended his record (Hulhulé airport projects, the expanded list of 26 basic food items) while the MDP questioned the dollar shortage, slower economic growth and budget increases; the chair cautioned one speaker about making claims that could defame someone. The Majlis then rejected, at the acceptance stage, an MDP resolution objecting to the government taking 14 plots of land away from Malé City Council, and in the vote the no-confidence motion against Minister Saeed also failed. Parts of the text are jumbled but the votes are clearly recorded.

items.title: No-confidence motion against Minister of Economic Development, Transport and Trade Mohamed Saeed (Constitution Art. 101(a), Rule 229(a)), signed by 13 MPs

items.title: Resolution seeking MPs' view on the government decision to remove 14 plots of land from Malé City Council's jurisdiction and make them state property
Votes on matters that reached the voting stage
items.outcome: no-confidence motion in Minister Mohamed Saeed not passed 10-54

speakers.name: Mohamed Saeed
positions: Said exchange-rate policy is the Maldives Monetary Authority's legal duty, and dollars released at the official rate have risen about 97-100% compared with the previous government.
Said the commercial port is moving to Thilafushi, with full operation targeted for November 2027, and the essential goods list is growing from 3 to 26 and then 80 items.
Said bunkering earned USD 90.07 million, no business centre was closed, 313 investments have been registered since November 2023, and townships must invest at least USD 500 million and pay taxes.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the Thilafushi commercial port project started in 2020 and its second phase in 2023, both under the MDP government, not this one.
Noted that the Finance Minister said 2026 growth fell from a projected 5.7% to 0.6%, and questioned the minister on the dollar rate and large budget increases.
Said decisions on basic food items were made through late-night phone calls rather than formally in cabinet.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Raised a point of order saying the issue was the dollar rate reaching 23, not Presidents Nasheed or Solih; the chair ruled it was not a point of order.
Presented a resolution objecting to the housing ministry taking 14 Malé City Council plots without consulting the council or giving project details.
Argued the move weakens decentralisation, breaks consultation steps in the Decentralisation Act, and cuts council income used for parks, mosques and administration.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the MDP-majority parliament initially declined to approve Saeed for cabinet, and PNC members secured his approval.
Attributed dollar shortages to about USD 1.2 billion a year in debt repayments against about USD 1.5 billion in revenue, and said exchange matters fall to the MMA.
Rejected opposition calls for a referendum on the Rasmaale project, citing past resort lease extensions done without referendums.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said none of the motion's points justify no-confidence and that the dollar black market existed under the previous MDP government.
Blamed the MDP government's money printing and unproductive loans for the dollar rate, and urged members to focus on the budget instead.
Said all 73 members of the PNC parliamentary group have full confidence in the minister.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Presented the motion, saying the black-market dollar rate passed MVR 21 and Malé port congestion raised prices.
Said investor forums in Dubai, India, Malaysia, Singapore and the UK cost large sums but produced no disclosed investment, and the Development Bank spent MVR 6.56 million without opening.
Said SEZ amendments creating townships and a 'Maldives Pearl Residence' programme put sovereignty at risk, and announced megaprojects such as MIFC have stalled.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Backed the minister as the most capable for the post, crediting him with SME banking, business incubators, bunkering and townships.
Urged MDP members not to take up parliament's time with motions he described as baseless.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said he has full confidence in the minister, citing his work to keep essential goods available during the global crisis.
Said dollar issues in the motion are not directly the minister's responsibility and need study of debt payments and dollar earners.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said GDP growth is forecast at 0.6%, and food inflation is 7.38% in 2025 and 8.59% so far in 2026, contradicting the minister's claim that food prices are falling.
Said announced projects such as the USD 8.8 billion MIFC, a floating solar city and the Uthuru Thilafalhu agricultural zone have shown no progress.
Raised concern that the townships could host other faiths and argued the President himself appears to lack confidence in the minister.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Called the motion a personally motivated attack on a hard-working minister, citing Saeed's tourism experience and eight years as economic minister; continues into part 2.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the no-confidence motion has no real basis and the MDP is upset Saeed did not serve as its own economic minister.
Credited the government with lowering staple food prices and argued the dollar rate worsened under the MDP government; said he trusts Minister Saeed.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Raised a point of order saying a member was deliberately misleading the public about the minister's remarks; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

decisions: The Speaker announced the no-confidence motion against Minister Mohamed Saeed would be debated, then put to a vote at the day's voting time.
Per General Committee advice, debate was set at 2 hours: 1 hour for the minister's defence and 1 hour for members (PNC 38 min, MDP 9, MDA 3, JP 3, MNP 3, independents 2 each).
The sitting recessed from 10:31 to 11:00, and the Speaker said the sitting would close with votes once the agenda was finished.
The chair ruled the South Galolhu member's intervention was not a point of order.
Debate on the no-confidence motion against Minister Mohamed Saeed closed; vote held at the day's voting time.
Resolution on the 14 Malé City Council plots was not accepted (11 for, 52 against), so its work ended.
Motion of no confidence in Minister of Economic Development, Transport and Trade Mohamed Saeed failed (10 for, 54 against; 47 needed).
Next sitting announced for Monday 9 November 2026 at 9:00 am.
